Action Plan:
1. Arrange same-day face-to-face review at the central London clinic for physical examination.
2. Following examination, perform blood tests: thick & thin blood films for malaria, full blood count, inflammatory markers (e.g., CRP/ESR), liver & renal profile.  
3. If unable to attend the clinic promptly, patient to present to nearest Emergency Department with copy of clinician’s notes for identical work-up.  
4. Advise patient to refrain from work (nursing duties) until assessment and investigations completed. Provide medical certificate if required.  
5. Admin team to contact patient and book the clinic slot; patient to ring provided number within a few minutes to confirm appointment.  
6. Safety-net: If symptoms worsen (persisting fever, rigors, confusion, rash, reduced urine output), patient to present to ED immediately.  
7. Chronic back pain: continue physiotherapy exercises and posture training; no change to current plan today.  
8. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for call: 7-day history of fever with alternating chills/rigors, generalized myalgia, night sweats, nausea, reduced oral intake, fatigue.  
• No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, neck stiffness, focal headaches, urinary symptoms, or rash.  
• Travel: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; extensive rural trekking and cycling; took daily malaria prophylaxis (exact drug and regimen uncertain, reportedly “another one on top of the first”).  
• Past medical history: Chronic mechanical back pain (under physiotherapy).  
• Family history: Father died of myocardial infarction age 68.  
• Medications: Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented); recent OTC paracetamol and ibuprofen at recommended doses.  
• Allergies: Seasonal pollen (hay fever); no drug allergies reported.  
• Social: Registered nurse; non-smoker; moderate alcohol; exercises moderately several times per week; up-to-date occupational vaccinations (incl. Hep B).

Objective:
• Telephone consult only – no physical examination or vitals performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Pyrexia of unknown origin post-travel
   - Assessment: Acute febrile illness; need to exclude malaria and other tropical infections versus common bacterial/viral causes.
   - Differential: Malaria, dengue, enteric fever, viral illness, influenza-like illness, COVID-19, occult bacterial infection.
   - Investigations planned: Thick & thin blood films x3 over 24 h, FBC, U&Es, LFTs, CRP/ESR, blood cultures, urinalysis; further tests per in-person findings.
   - Treatment: Supportive (hydration, antipyretics); definitive therapy guided by results.
   - Referrals: GP clinic same day; ED if unable to attend or clinical deterioration.

2. Fitness for work
   - Assessment: Currently unfit for nursing duties due to febrile illness and pending investigations.
   - Treatment: Advise leave from work; issue medical certificate after clinic review.

3. Chronic mechanical back pain
   - Assessment: Stable; managed with physiotherapy.
   - Treatment: Continue current physio exercises and posture correction; no new interventions today.
   - Referral: None at this time.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Vital signs, physical examination findings, COVID-19 vaccination status, detailed medication list with doses, drug allergies confirmation.  
● Internal conflicts: None detected.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; minimal background noise; minor repetitions but clinically complete.
